h1: 3D rendering for Islamabad developers, architects and product brands
intro: 22 Signals produces 3D rendering for Islamabad developers, architects, interior designers and product brands: photoreal exteriors, interiors, walkthrough animations, product and packaging renders, and 3D models for web and ads. We work from your drawings, match approved plans, and deliver images ready for brochures, hoardings, websites and campaigns.

sections.h: Selling buildings that do not exist yet
p: Much of Islamabad's property market sells before construction: apartments in towers going up along the Expressway, commercial plazas in new markaz areas, farmhouses and villas around Gulberg Greens. Buyers, often including overseas Pakistanis deciding from abroad, judge the project on images. If the renders look amateur, so does the project. If they look nothing like the final building, trust disappears at handover.

That is the balance 3D rendering has to strike. Islamabad buyers want to see the project at its best, and they also want it faithful to the plans, materials and surroundings that will really be there.

p: Buyers in the capital have learned to check whether a project is approved by the Capital Development Authority, or by the Rawalpindi Development Authority on the other side of the twin city. We ask for the approved drawings before we start, render what has been approved, and label images as artist's impressions. Where a design is still in approval, we mark the renders as concepts.
This protects your buyers and your reputation, and it keeps your marketing consistent with what your sales team can actually promise.

sections.h: Beyond property: product and technical work
p: Not every Islamabad client sells real estate. Software and hardware companies need product visuals for pitch decks and trade shows. Health tech startups need clean renders of devices that are still prototypes. Telecom and infrastructure suppliers need technical images for tenders and proposals. 3D rendering produces all of these without waiting for a finished product or booking a studio.

Hardware founders around the National Incubation Center often need renders for an investor deck long before the first production unit exists. A clean model also gives you exploded views, colour options and packaging mock-ups from the same file.

Once a 3D model exists, it can do more than one job. The same model produces stills for the brochure, a walkthrough for YouTube, short clips for Instagram and an interactive view for your website. Planning this from the start costs less than commissioning each piece separately, and keeps every visual consistent.

Much of the 3D rendering Islamabad developers commission ends up on WhatsApp, forwarded by agents to buyers in the Gulf, the UK and North America. We export versions sized for phone screens and quick sharing, alongside the full-resolution files for print and hoardings.

p: We have worked with more than 30 companies, from property and retail to healthcare and technology. Rendering for clients in different markets has taught us to ask early about local materials, light and surroundings, because a render that looks right in one city can look wrong in another. For 3D rendering, Islamabad has its own details to get right: the Margalla Hills on the skyline, the hard summer light and the green belts between sectors.

sections.h: Working with us from Islamabad, and cost factors
p: You send CAD or Revit files, drawings, material samples and site photos; we send drafts for review with comments marked on the image. Feedback calls are booked at times that suit your team, and each round of changes has a date agreed in writing. Site visits in Islamabad happen when the project needs it.

We do not publish prices for 3D rendering. Islamabad projects are costed on the number of views, the level of detail, interiors versus exteriors, animation length, how complete your drawings are, and the number of revision rounds.

We do more than render. The same team can build the project website, run the ad campaigns, and produce the launch video, so your visuals arrive with a plan to sell. Related: video production and animation in Islamabad, paid media, and our global 3D rendering service.

faqs.q: What files do you need to start a render?
faqs.a: Ideally CAD, Revit or SketchUp files, plus elevations, sections and a materials list. If you only have PDF drawings, we can model from those. Site photos help us place the building in its real surroundings, including the Margalla Hills backdrop when it is in view. The more complete the inputs, the fewer revision rounds you need.

faqs.q: Can renders match our approved plans exactly?
faqs.a: Yes, and we recommend it. We render from the approved drawings, label images as artist's impressions and mark anything still in design as a concept. If plans change, we update the model rather than starting again, so your marketing stays accurate as the project moves forward.

Yes. Once the 3D model exists, we can produce walkthroughs, flythroughs and short social clips from it, with music and captions in English or Urdu. Many developers use one model for brochure stills, a YouTube walkthrough and Instagram clips, which keeps everything consistent.

faqs.q: Can you render interiors for show apartments?
faqs.a: Yes. Interior renders are often used before a show unit is built, or instead of one. We work with your interior designer's specification, or propose a style that fits the target buyer, and render each room with realistic materials and lighting.

faqs.q: Do you visit sites in Islamabad?
faqs.a: Most rendering work is done from drawings and photos, which you or your team can take. If a site visit would genuinely improve the result, for example for a complex masterplan in Islamabad, we arrange it when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Do you render projects in Rawalpindi as well as Islamabad?
faqs.a: Yes. We render projects across the twin city and beyond, from towers in Islamabad's newer sectors to housing schemes on the Rawalpindi side. The process is the same: approved drawings, material references and site photos. We match the renders to the actual surroundings, so a project in Rawalpindi does not end up with an Islamabad skyline behind it.

We agree the number of revision rounds before work starts and put it in writing with the schedule. Clear inputs and a single point of approval on your side keep rounds to a minimum. Extra rounds are possible, and we tell you the effect on time before we start them.
